title: Trajectory SLO Prober: multi-protocol streaming load harness with regression classifier
creator: Luca Moreno
description: Build a scalable, multi-protocol (SSE + WebSocket) streaming load harness that exercises chat/completions traffic shapes and classifies SLO regressions automatically. The harness (Trajectory SLO Prober) will generate realistic user trajectories (short chitchat -> long completion -> streaming tool calls), warm and exercise KV cache behavior, and surface token/sec, p95 latency, and tail anomalies per-model and per-tenant. It must support tenant isolation, burst windows, policy-driven fallback to cheaper model variants, and be runnable both from our k8s perf cluster and locally for dev debugging. The goal is to detect regressions introduced by runtime changes (kernel swaps, quantization profiles, batching adjustments) with statistical confidence and create actionable alerts and reproduction artifacts (replay sessions + reproducible seed).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can spawn 50k concurrent simulated sessions (mix of SSE + WS) in perf-cluster mode
Per-tenant p95 and tokens/sec computed and emitted every 30s to observability pipeline
Regression classifier raises an alert when p95 increases by >=10% with >=95% confidence compared to baseline
Generated minimal reproducer (session trace + prompts + seed) for any alerted regression
Integration tests for SSE and WS client flows with KV cache warmup in CI (smoke tier)
Grafana dashboards and alert rule documented with runbook entry and Slack channel integration
implementation_notes: Core harness written in Go for low-variance timing and easy k8s integration; small orchestration shim in Python for experiment definitions
Client primitives: SSE client that respects keep-alive and cancellation; duplex WebSocket client supporting multiplexed user sessions
Token emission uses deterministic token stream generator seeded per-session to produce reproducible token counts and token-time distributions
KV cache warmup stage: simulate prefix-only sessions to build prefix/KV entries before main experiment window
Statistical approach: use bootstrap-based comparison of p95 distributions across windows, with configurable alpha and minimum sample sizes
Support synthetic error injection (latency spikes, 500s) to validate classifier sensitivity
Expose experiment ABI (YAML) with workload mix, client mix, session journey graphs, tenant quotas and fallback policies
CLI supports dry-run, scale-plan output, and upload of generated metrics artifacts to perf-artifacts S3
qa_plan: Unit tests for deterministic stream generator (coverage >90%)
Local dev mode: small cluster with 100 sessions to validate protocol and KV warmup
Staged run in perf cluster: 1k -> 10k -> 50k sessions to validate autoscaling and telemetry
Inject controlled regressions from runtime changes (e.g., change kernel selector) and verify classifier alerts
Post-run reconciliation: ensure produced reproducer replays to same p95 within 5% on a dedicated debug node
risks: High load runs could interfere with production-adjacent clusters if scheduling not isolated; require node taints and namespace quotas
False positives if workload mix differs significantly from baseline; need to version baseline and annotate experiments
Large non-determinism from upstream model runtimes (stochastic sampling) may increase noise; mitigations: use deterministic sampling or model variants that support temperature=0
Resource footprint could be substantial during 50k session runs; add cost estimation and preflight checks
